hypothesis: Champion recipe (stable PGO + THP) on the x86 boxes. Stable PGO was previously blocked by a rustc LLVM SIGILL while instrumenting the reth crate, but that was rustc 1.99.1 and these boxes now run 1.100.0 — so try stable before falling back to the nightly workaround. Measured against the same-harness stock baselines.
llm_commentary: Two results in one run. First: x86_64 PGO now builds on STABLE rustc. The blocker was a SIGILL inside libLLVM while instrumenting the reth crate on 1.99.1; these boxes run 1.100.0 and all five x86 families built and measured without the nightly workaround, so PGO no longer needs an unstable toolchain — which is what made it a plausible release-build proposal rather than a lab trick. Second: on the workload metric the full stack (4 code commits + PGO + THP) measures -21.9% to -40.8% across 8 instance types, against the -14% to -29% the old wall-clock metric reported for the code commits alone. New overall best is m8azn-3xl at 2.98s, with c8a at 3.04s for a third of the cost per run ($0.000364 vs $0.001025). The phase split explains the ordering: heavy falls 30-48% everywhere (storage path plus PGO), while light barely moves on the fast Zen 5 boxes (c8a 0.94->0.99s, i.e. slightly worse) and improves most on the slower cores (i8g 2.41->1.77s). On c8a the light phase is now ~1s for 200k calls, which is close to what the co-located oha client can drive, so that phase is likely measuring the load generator rather than the server — harness item 3 (move the client off-box) is the prerequisite for trusting light-phase numbers on the fastest hardware.
